title: Farlands Remastered
description: Brings Far Lands-style terrain back to modern Paper servers, starting at ±12,550,821 blocks in the normal Overworld.
body:
# Farlands Remastered

**Farlands Reborn** is a Paper server plugin that brings Far Lands-inspired terrain generation back to modern Minecraft.

The plugin works as a custom world generator for the normal Overworld. The world generates normally until players reach the classic Far Lands distance around **±12,550,821 blocks**. Beyond that point, newly generated chunks begin to form broken terrain inspired by old Minecraft Beta Far Lands: huge vertical walls, holes, overhangs, repeated noise patterns, and chaotic terrain shapes.

This plugin does **not** add commands, items, mobs, dimensions, or gameplay systems. Its only purpose is to change terrain generation beyond the Far Lands border.

## Features

- Far Lands-style terrain starting at **±12,550,821**
- Works in the normal Overworld
- No commands
- No extra dimensions
- No NMS
- Terrain can generate up to **Y=319**
- Configurable generation settings

## Installation for server

- Download the plugin `.jar` file.
- Put the `.jar` file into your server's `plugins` folder.
- Open `bukkit.yml` in the main server folder.
- Add this generator setting:

```yaml
worlds:
  world:
    generator: FarLandsPaper
```

- Restart the server.

## Important

Already generated chunks will not change.  
For the best result, create a new world or delete the already generated world folders before starting the server.

For the default world name, delete these folders:

```text
world
world_nether
world_the_end
```

If your world name is different, open `server.properties` and check this line:

```properties
level-name=world
```

Then use that world name in `bukkit.yml`.

Example:

```properties
level-name=Survival
```

Then your `bukkit.yml` should look like this:

```yaml
worlds:
  Survival:
    generator: FarLandsPaper
```

## Testing

After installation, teleport to the Far Lands area:

```text
/tp <player> 12550900 160 0
```

Far Lands-style terrain starts after approximately:

```text
X/Z ±12,550,821
```
